- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; especially after recent spikes.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction by 2–5% of forecast range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per period unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is bearish (≥ 0.67) and model is flat or rising, force downward adjustment — especially if supply net is negative and events are neutral or bearish.
- Mean reversion applies if price deviates >15% from 30-day moving average — adjust forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast by 1–3% per event if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period to avoid false bullish momentum.
